knowledge.amplitudeHelp: Largest oscillation of the measurement you accept in normal operation. Unlocks: oscillation amplitude check.
knowledge.delayHelp: Time between a change of the controller output and the first visible reaction of the measurement. Unlocks: Harris index.
knowledge.error: Could not use the loop data: {reason}
knowledge.howToAmplitude: Take it from the process: the largest peak-to-peak swing of the measurement that quality, safety or downstream units still tolerate. Enter it in the measurement's engineering units.
knowledge.howToDelay: Put the controller in manual and make a small step in the output (2-5 %). Read the time from the step to the first clear movement of the measurement, away from noise. Repeat in both directions and take the larger value.
knowledge.howToRanges: Use the calibrated span of the transmitter (0 % and 100 % of the signal) and of the final element. Values may be zero or negative, for example -50 to 150 degC or a vacuum pressure.
knowledge.howToUltimate: With the controller in auto and integral action removed, raise the gain until the measurement oscillates steadily, or take the period from a peak-to-peak time of an existing sustained oscillation in the trend. Measure several cycles and average.
knowledge.intro: The analysis needs a few facts about this loop. Without them it skips the checks that depend on them. The values are saved in the project file (project.json) of this dataset on this computer; nothing is sent to the plant.
knowledge.invalidRange: Enter a number (zero and negative values are allowed).
knowledge.kindExample: A flotation cell level is integrating: if the outlet valve is opened 5 % more than the inflow needs, the level falls steadily until the valve is moved back. A flow or a temperature is self-regulating: after an output step it settles at a new value.
knowledge.kindHelp: Integrating: the measurement keeps ramping after an output change and does not settle by itself, like a tank level. Self-regulating: it settles at a new value.
knowledge.rangeInverted: The {range} minimum must be lower than its maximum.
knowledge.rangeOutMissing: The output tag has no engineering range, so saturation and valve numbers cannot be assessed. Set the range on the output tag.
knowledge.rangePvMissing: The measurement tag has no engineering range; the amplitude limit must then be entered by hand.
knowledge.rangesPrecedence: A value here overrides the tag dictionary. Leave a field blank to use the dictionary value (shown in grey).
knowledge.title: Loop data
knowledge.ultimateHelp: Period of the loop's natural oscillation when it is pushed to the edge of stability. Needed together with the amplitude limit.
knowledge.vendorHelp: The Tuning tab then lists the parameter names of this block, with the values to type in. Nothing is written to the controller.

tuning.ipdt.action.no_out_move: Choose a window where the output was moved, or run a step test: in manual, change the output by a few percent and record.
tuning.ipdt.action.post_move_too_short: Record longer after the last output move, or end the window later.
tuning.ipdt.action.pre_move_lead_under_2: Start the window earlier, with a quiet stretch of level before the first output move.
tuning.ipdt.action.r2_below_0.8: Choose a window with one clear output step and a steady inflow. If the level settles after the step, set the process type to self-regulating.
tuning.ipdt.action.slope_se_over_20pct: Repeat the step with a larger move or a longer record.
tuning.ipdt.action.theta_on_grid_edge: Use a window with a sharper output step, or check that the PV and OUT timestamps line up.
tuning.ipdt.action.unknown: Choose another window or record a new step test.
tuning.ipdt.action.up_down_differ_over_2: Check the valve for asymmetry or repeat the test in both directions.
tuning.ipdt.delayWide: The dead-time range is wide: the dead time is uncertain. Record a longer or larger output step to narrow it.
tuning.ipdt.experimental: Level-loop tuning is experimental: in simulation, 3 of 270 accepted fits (slow integrators with an underestimated dead time) gave an unsafe controller, so this version uses the upper bound of the dead time; check the proposed settings on the preview and apply them with care.
tuning.ipdt.explain: Integrating process: the level ramps after an output step, so there is no gain and time constant. The slope is how fast the level changes per second for each 1 % of output.
tuning.ipdt.lowConfidence: Low confidence: the settings are given, but treat them with care.
tuning.ipdt.overshoot: Setpoint overshoot is expected with these settings: a PI controller on an integrating process overshoots after a setpoint step. They are chosen for steady level control and disturbance rejection; use small setpoint changes or a setpoint ramp if overshoot matters.
tuning.ipdt.reason.no_out_move: The controller output did not move in this window.
tuning.ipdt.reason.post_move_too_short: Too little record after the last output move (needs at least five dead times and 300 s).
tuning.ipdt.reason.pre_move_lead_under_2: The output moves too early: less than a fifth of the window comes before the first move.
tuning.ipdt.reason.r2_below_0.8: The ramp does not describe this window well (R² below 0.8).
tuning.ipdt.reason.theta_on_grid_edge: The dead-time estimate hit the edge of the search range, so it cannot be trusted.
tuning.ipdt.reason.unknown: The fit was refused for a reason this screen does not know.
tuning.ipdt.reason.up_down_differ_over_2: The slope after an increase and after a decrease of the output differ by more than 25 %.
tuning.ipdt.reverse: The level falls when the output rises (negative slope). Set the controller to reverse the action (direct acting); the vendor form already carries this.
tuning.model.ratioEasy: Dead time is short compared with the time constant: easy to control.
tuning.model.ratioHard: Dead time is longer than the time constant: hard to control with PI; prefer a smooth, slow tuning.
tuning.model.ratioMedium: Dead time is comparable to the time constant: moderate; keep the tuning smooth.

tuning.recommendation: Proposal (SIMC rule): Kc = {kc}, Ti = {ti} s. {fit} Enter the values by hand after review, change one setting at a time and watch the loop.
tuning.recommendation.ipdt: Proposal (SIMC rule for an integrating process): Kc = {kc}, Ti = {ti} s, closed-loop time constant tau_c = {tauc} s. Integrating process: the level ramps after an output step. {fit} The settings are computed with the upper bound of the dead-time range ({upper} s), which is conservative: slow ramps make the dead time uncertain. Enter the values by hand after review, change one setting at a time and watch the loop.
tuning.swing.intro: To let the level swing within a limit instead of using the robustness slider, give both values. Leave both empty otherwise.
tuning.swing.invalid.both: Give both values or leave both empty.
tuning.swing.result: With this limit the closed-loop time constant is tau_c = {tauc} s.

tuning.warning.closed_loop_data: The window contains closed-loop (auto) data, so the model can be biased. Prefer a step test with the loop in manual.
tuning.warning.looks_integrating: This loop is marked self-regulating, but it behaves like an integrator (the level ramps after an output step).
tuning.warning.looks_integrating.model_f: A first-order model could not be fitted, but a ramp model fits well (R² {r2}).
tuning.warning.looks_integrating.time_co: The fitted time constant ({tau} s) is more than three times the window length.
tuning.warning.looks_self_regulating: This loop is marked integrating, but the ramp does not fit while a first-order model does (R² {r2}). Check the process type in the loop knowledge.
tuning.warning.setIntegratingConfirm: This saves the process type of this loop as integrating in the dataset's project file (local configuration; nothing is written to the plant). The tuning is then recomputed with the integrating model.
tuning.window.invalid: The end must be after the start and inside the record.
tuning.window.none: No test window found: the loop was never in manual with output moves. The whole record is used; the result may be unreliable.
tuning.window.padded: Window extended by {before} s before and {after} s after the output moves so the quiet start and the settling are included
tuning.window.pickTitle: Or pick any window on the record
tuning.window.suggested: Suggested test windows (loop in manual, output moved)
tuning.window.useVisible: Use the visible range as the window
tuning.window.zoomHint: Drag on a chart to zoom in, then use the visible range. The suggested windows above are stretches where the loop was in manual and the output moved.
valve.banner: Nothing is written to the plant. The operator carries out the test by hand; this page prepares the procedure and analyses the record.
valve.check.abort: The abort rule is agreed: anyone may stop the test at any time and return the output to the starting value.
valve.check.manual: The loop may be put in MANUAL for the whole test without harming the process or the product.
valve.check.operator: The operator and the shift supervisor know about the test and agree to it.
valve.checklist.intro: Tick every point. The procedure is shown only after that.

valve.intro: A stroke test moves the controller output in small steps while the loop is in manual and measures when the valve starts to move (deadband) and how finely it can be positioned (resolution). The operator carries it out by hand: this page only prepares the procedure and analyses the record. Nothing is written to the plant.
valve.plan.recordHint: Log time, controller output and process value (about every 1 to 5 seconds) during the test.
valve.plan.step.abort: If anything looks wrong at any time, stop: return the output to {op} % and put the loop back in AUTO.
valve.plan.step.abortBand: If the process value moves more than {band} from its starting value, or if anything looks wrong at any time, stop: return the output to {op} % and put the loop back in AUTO.
valve.plan.step.return_auto: Return the output to {op} % and put the loop back in AUTO.
valve.plan.step.set_start: Set the output to {op} % and wait {dwell} s.
valve.plan.step.step: Set the output to {op} % and wait {dwell} s.
valve.plan.title: Operator procedure
valve.record.csvHelp: Columns: time in seconds (or an ISO date-time), controller output in % and process value. Header names such as t_s, op and pv are recognised; semicolons and decimal commas work. The file is read in your browser and sent only to the analysis service; it is not stored.
valve.record.fromCsv: The test is in a CSV file
valve.record.fromDataset: The test is in this dataset
valve.record.fromDatasetHelp: Choose the stretch of the record that contains the test.
valve.record.title: Analyse the record
valve.result.caveat: The estimates follow the ANSI/ISA-75.25.01 and ISA-TR75.25.02 definitions as recalled; the standards were not read. Treat the result as a screening, not as a certified test.
valve.result.incomplete.no_gain: The valve did not move the process value noticeably, so the deadband cannot be estimated. The valve may be stuck, or the steps may be too small for the process noise.
valve.result.incomplete.no_move_after_re: After the direction reversals the process value did not respond within a leg: the deadband is larger than the travel of one leg.
valve.result.pvLeftBand: The process value left the abort band during the test: the result may be affected.
valve.result.resolutionNone: not certified for the step sizes tested
valve.result.summaryDeadband: After a reversal the valve needs about {value} % of span of output change before it moves. A deadband of this size can cause limit cycles: check the valve and positioner before retuning.
valve.result.summaryGood: No significant deadband was found: the valve responded to small steps.
valve.result.title: Result
valve.settings.dwellHelp: How long each step is held. Use at least 3 times (dead time + time constant) of the loop so the process settles; 4 to 6 times is better.
valve.settings.opStartHelp: The output the loop has now, in manual. The test stays close to it.
valve.settings.pvBandHelp: The operator stops and returns to the starting output if the process value moves further than this from its starting value. Leave blank for no abort band.
valve.settings.stepSizes: Step sizes (% of span, comma separated)
valve.settings.stepSizesHelp: Default: 1 and 0.25. Each size is run up, down and up again.
valve.title: Valve stroke test
